message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run** example of how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
The example uses the `gcloud` CLI, but I also show the equivalent REST‑API request so you can integrate it into your own tooling.

> **Prerequisites**
> * You have a Google Cloud project with billing enabled.
> * The Compute Engine API is enabled (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`).
> * You have sufficient GPU quota in the zone you plan to use.
> * You have the `gcloud` CLI installed and authenticated (`gcloud auth login`).

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Variables – replace with your own values
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # choose a zone that supports RTX A6000
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
    --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
    --zone="$ZONE" \
    --machine-type="n1-highmem-8" \            # 8 vCPU, 61 GB RAM – adjust as needed
    --accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1" \
    --image-family="ubuntu-2004-lts" \
    --image-project="ubuntu-os-cloud" \
    --boot-disk-size="50GB" \
    --boot-disk-type="pd-standard" \
    --maintenance-policy="MIGRATE" \
    --scopes="https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform" \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional: custom init script
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU & memory configuration. Use a type that supports GPUs (e.g., `n1-highmem-8`). |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Specifies Ubuntu 20.04 LTS. |
| `--boot-disk-size` / `--boot-disk-type` | Disk size & type. |
| `--maintenance-policy` | Keeps the VM running during maintenance events. |
| `--scopes` | Grants the VM full Cloud Platform access (adjust if you need tighter scopes). |

---

## 2. Using the REST API

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine API directly (e.g., from a script or CI/CD pipeline), here’s the exact JSON payload you’d POST to:

```http
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/machineTypes/n1-highmem-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 50,
        "diskType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/diskTypes/pd-standard"
      }
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y cuda-toolkit-11-7"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Replace `{PROJECT_ID}` and `{ZONE}` with your actual project ID and zone.  
Make sure you have an OAuth 2.0 access token with the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform` scope.

---

## 3. Quick sanity check

After the instance starts, you can SSH into it and verify the GPU:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu --zone=$ZONE
$ nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version and CUDA support.

---

### Need more help?

* **GPU availability** – Check which zones support the RTX A6000:  
  `gcloud compute accelerator-types list --filter="type:nvidia-tesla-a6000" --format="table(name,zone)"`

* **Quota** – View your current GPU quota:  
  `gcloud compute regions describe $REGION --format="json(gpus)"`

Feel free to ask if you need a script that automates the entire workflow or if you run into any errors!
